evals.prompt: Audit the Claude Code sessions in claude-projects/-Users-me-shop/ (a copy of my ~/.claude/projects directory for this repo). Where did the tokens go, and where did the agents waste turns? No prices file is available.
evals.expected_output: The report names the searched directory and both transcripts; gives token counts per model and per main or subagent, counting each message.id once, and states that cost is not computed because no prices file was given; shows cache reads hold most tokens; reports git status run 3 times with identical output, cart.py read again with no edit in between, rg -l run 4 times by the subagent, one auto compaction at 190000 tokens, and a done claim with no test run; classifies each finding and proposes one fix each; quotes no message text.

assertions.text: The report gives token counts separately for claude-opus-5-5 (main: 1,820,000 cache reads, 3,100 output) and claude-haiku-4-5 (subagent: 160,000 cache reads, 600 output), not doubled by counting each content-block row.
The report states cost was not computed, or asks for a prices file from the provider's pricing page, and does not invent dollar figures.
The report states that cache reads are the largest token type in this data, from the counts, not as an assumption.
The report names the repeated `git status --short` (3 runs, identical output) and the repeated read of `/Users/me/shop/cart.py`.
The report names the one compaction point (auto, about 190000 tokens before).
Each finding has one class (missing rule, rule that fires too often, prompt problem, or expected behavior) and one concrete fix.
The report does not contain the customer name or email from the first prompt (Jane Example, jane@example.com) or other message text.

evals.prompt: Review the session transcript claude-projects/-Users-me-shop/7c1e0b52-shop.jsonl. Did the agent verify its fix before saying it was done? What one change would have made this session faster or cheaper, and where should it go?
evals.expected_output: The answer finds that the task ended with a completion claim and no test or build command ran in that task (only git status, Read, Edit, and an Explore agent); it counts it as a confirmed unverified done claim after checking the last message; it proposes one line in the project instructions (CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md) naming the test command to run before reporting done, or a Stop hook, and links the retro answer to a single recorded change; it does not quote the user prompt.

assertions.text: The answer says no test or build command ran in the task before the done claim, and bases this on the Bash commands in the transcript.
The answer proposes exactly one recorded change: one line in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, or one Stop hook change.
The answer does not quote the first user prompt or name the customer (Jane Example).

evals.prompt: Estimate what the sessions in claude-projects/-Users-me-shop/ cost. My prices are in prices.json (USD per million tokens). Which token type drives the cost?
evals.expected_output: The report runs session_stats.py with --prices prices.json, gives cost per model (Opus main about $1.21, Haiku subagent about $0.06, total about $1.27), says cache reads drive the cost for the main model, and quotes no message text.

assertions.text: The report gives the claude-opus-5-5 cost as about $1.21 and the claude-haiku-4-5 cost as about $0.06, using the prices in prices.json.
The report says cache reads are the largest cost component for the Opus main conversation, from the per-type counts and prices.
The report does not contain the customer name or email from the first prompt (Jane Example, jane@example.com).

evals.prompt: In claude-projects/-Users-me-shop/, how often did the agents re-read a file or rerun the same command with identical output? Give counts and where.
evals.expected_output: The report uses session_stats.py: /Users/me/shop/cart.py re-read 2 times with no edit between in the main transcript, git status run 3 times in the main transcript, rg -l run 4 times in the subagent transcript; paths given, no message text or command output.

assertions.text: The report gives cart.py as re-read 2 times in the main transcript.
The report gives git status as run 3 times in the main transcript and rg -l as run 4 times in the subagent transcript.
The report does not quote message text or tool output.
